title: Why Ice Floats
subject: phys
paras: Most substances become denser when they freeze. Their particles slow down and pack more tightly together, so a solid piece usually sinks in its own liquid. A block of solid wax, for example, sinks to the bottom of a pot of melted wax. Water is an unusual exception to this rule.

A water molecule is made of one oxygen atom and two hydrogen atoms. The molecule has a slight negative charge on the oxygen side and slight positive charges on the hydrogen side. Because opposite charges attract, neighboring molecules pull on one another and form weak links called hydrogen bonds.

In liquid water, these bonds constantly break and re-form, and the molecules can crowd close together. When water freezes, however, each molecule locks into place and bonds with four neighbors in a fixed pattern. This pattern is an open, six-sided structure with a lot of empty space inside it. As a result, ice takes up about nine percent more space than the same amount of liquid water, and it is less dense.

This simple fact has large effects on life. When a lake freezes in winter, the ice forms at the surface and floats there. The layer of ice works like a blanket, slowing the loss of heat from the water below. Fish and other organisms can survive in the liquid water under the ice until spring. If ice sank, many lakes might freeze solid from the bottom up.

The expansion of freezing water also shapes the land. Water seeps into cracks in rocks, freezes at night, and pushes the cracks wider. Over many years, this process, called frost wedging, can break large rocks into smaller pieces.

qs.q: According to paragraph 1, what usually happens when a substance freezes?
opts: It becomes denser and sinks in its liquid.
qs.why: 第1段：Most substances become denser when they freeze… a solid piece usually sinks in its own liquid.

qs.q: The word "exception" in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to
opts: a case that does not follow the rule
qs.why: exception 指不符合规则的情况，上文正是在讲一般规律。

qs.q: According to paragraph 2, why do water molecules attract one another?
opts: They have opposite charges on different sides.
qs.why: Because opposite charges attract, neighboring molecules pull on one another.

qs.q: The word "it" in paragraph 3 ("and it is less dense") refers to
qs.why: ice takes up about nine percent more space…, and it is less dense —— it 指 ice。

qs.q: What can be inferred from paragraph 4 about a lake in which ice sank?
opts: It would stay warmer all winter.
More of its water might freeze, harming the organisms in it.
It would never freeze at all.
qs.why: If ice sank, many lakes might freeze solid from the bottom up —— 生物将难以存活。

qs.q: Why does the author mention "frost wedging" in paragraph 5?
opts: To give an example of how the expansion of freezing water affects rocks
To explain why lakes freeze at the surface
To show that ice is denser than water
To describe how fish survive the winter
qs.why: 第5段讲结冰膨胀对地貌的作用，frost wedging 是具体例子。
